title: Expected four-stroke airflow from displacement, RPM and VE
graphPattern: During a clean WOT pull, MAF and RPM should rise together and calculated load should approach the profile's normal high-load range.
diagnosticUse: Low measured MAF versus expected airflow is a core signal for intake restriction, exhaust restriction, cam timing/compression loss, underboost or MAF under-reporting. It is never used alone; MAP, throttle, trims and ignition timing decide the branch.
recommendedChecks: Compare peak MAF to engine displacement and RPM
Check MAP/load coherence
Check WOT throttle opening
Compare fuel trims at idle, cruise and WOT

title: Separate idle trims from load trims
formula: combined_trim = STFT + LTFT; trim_load_delta = trim_load - trim_idle
graphPattern: If positive trim is high at idle but falls toward normal at 1500-2500 RPM or load, the extra air is a larger fraction of total airflow at idle.
diagnosticUse: This pattern prioritizes unmetered air, vacuum leaks, PCV and EVAP purge leaks. If positive trims stay high under load, fuel delivery, MAF under-reporting or exhaust oxygen bias becomes more likely.
recommendedChecks: Smoke test intake and PCV/EVAP paths
Pinch EVAP purge hose only as a short diagnostic test where safe
Verify fuel pressure and MAF plausibility before replacing O2/A/F sensors

title: Use mirrored STFT/LTFT behavior to confirm a fuel-trim repair
graphPattern: After fixing a vacuum leak without clearing adaptations, a previously positive LTFT may be offset by negative STFT until LTFT relearns toward zero.
diagnosticUse: This prevents false failure calls immediately after repair. The important value is the sum of trims and its direction over time, not one stored LTFT snapshot.
recommendedChecks: Road-test after repair while watching STFT/LTFT together
Clear adaptations only when appropriate
Expect LTFT to step down gradually, not instantly on every ECU

title: Dirty MAF can over-report at idle and under-report at cruise/load
graphPattern: Negative fuel trim at idle with positive trim at cruise/load points toward a MAF that is biased differently across the airflow range.
diagnosticUse: This keeps the app from treating every positive trim as a fuel pump or every negative trim as a leaking injector. Range split plus VE mismatch raises MAF plausibility priority.
recommendedChecks: Repair downstream air leaks first
Verify O2/lambda response
Compare MAF curve to RPM and calculated VE
Check power, ground and signal voltage before replacement

title: Fuel delivery faults appear under load before idle
formula: load_lean_priority rises when trim_load is high, trim_idle is near normal, and power/airflow are low under WOT.
graphPattern: Idle trims can be acceptable while hard acceleration shows lean O2/lambda, high positive trim, low power and sometimes falling load.
diagnosticUse: Separates weak pump, restricted filter, low volume, regulator and injector delivery from small vacuum leaks.
recommendedChecks: Measure pressure and volume under load
Check pump voltage drop and ground
Compare commanded lambda to measured lambda
Do injector balance if one cylinder/bank pattern exists

title: Exhaust restriction is low airflow with high pumping loss
graphPattern: Throttle is high but MAF/VE and load are low, MAP stays high, RPM climb is slow and timing can be pulled back by heat/knock response.
diagnosticUse: Prioritizes catalytic converter, muffler, DPF on diesel, collapsed exhaust pipe or severe exhaust backpressure over a simple air-filter restriction.
recommendedChecks: Measure exhaust backpressure
Compare temperature before/after catalyst where applicable
Check MAP waveform on snap throttle
Do not condemn catalyst from P0420 alone

title: Heat reduces air density and can force ignition retard
graphPattern: High intake/coolant temperatures with late timing and reduced torque suggest thermal derate or knock-protection behavior.
diagnosticUse: Prevents mislabeling a hot-air or overheating power loss as a fuel fault when trims and airflow do not support that.
recommendedChecks: Verify ECT/IAT plausibility cold and hot
Check fans, thermostat, radiator and air pockets
Check fuel octane and knock sensor only after thermal conditions are understood

title: Low VE without trim direction suggests mechanical breathing
formula: mechanical_breathing_priority rises when VE and power are low but trims are not strongly lean/rich and intake/exhaust indices are weak.
graphPattern: The engine accepts throttle but never produces expected airflow or torque, while fuel control is not screaming in one direction.
diagnosticUse: Raises cam timing, VVT/VCT, compression, valve sealing, valve clearance, timing chain/belt and cylinder leakage checks.
recommendedChecks: Compression and leak-down test
Cam/crank correlation and VVT actual vs target
Idle vacuum/MAP waveform
Cylinder balance and misfire counters
